raw_response:
I'm 64 this year, farming alone on my 4.1 mu in Quzhou. I've done wheat-maize double cropping for 40 years, and I know this land. I only went to primary school, so I don't read books about farming — I do what experience tells me, and I watch what the neighbors do. My household is just me, so every yuan I spend on inputs is a yuan I don't have for medicine or food. I can't afford to take risks.

For wheat, I plant around **October 8–10**, same as every year. I save my own seed from the good ears — I cleaned them myself over the winter. Before planting, I hire the neighbor's boy to rotary-till the field with his small tractor. I spread about **80 jin of compound fertilizer per mu** as base fertilizer, then plant. In March when the wheat greens up, if it looks yellow I'll spread another **20 jin of urea per mu**; if it looks green enough, I might skip it to save money. I'll irrigate **three times**: the wintering water before freeze-up, once at jointing, and once at grain filling if it stays dry. The pump electricity isn't cheap, but wheat needs water to make grain. I'll spray herbicide once in spring if the weeds are bad — I walk the field with my backpack sprayer. I don't hire labor for this; I do the spreading and irrigating myself, though my back isn't what it used to be. I expect around **380 kg per mu** if the weather holds.

Maize is harder because the window is so tight. As soon as the wheat comes off in early June, I hire a combine, then get the maize in the ground within two or three days — no time to plow. I buy **hybrid seed** every year, about 3 jin per mu, because you can't save hybrid seed. I put down about **80 jin of compound fertilizer plus 20 jin of urea per mu**, all at planting. I don't side-dress anymore — I'm too old to walk through tall corn carrying a basket on my back. If it doesn't rain, I'll irrigate **twice**: once when the plants are small and once at flowering. I'll spray herbicide and maybe insecticide for corn borer if I see damage. I expect about **420 kg per mu** for the maize.

My total spending on seeds, fertilizer, pesticide, and irrigation will be about **2,900 yuan** this year. That's a lot for one old woman, but I need the grain to eat and to sell for cash. I don't try new things — I do what I've always done, what my neighbors do. Change is for younger people with money to lose.
